subtopics.title: Reading a Formula Like a Sentence

questions.question: In cost = R450 + R12,50 × km, the R450 represents:
options: The fixed charge, owed regardless of distance

questions.question: The R12,50 in the formula is:
options: The rate — the amount each kilometre adds to the bill

questions.question: In this formula, cost is called the DEPENDENT variable because:
options: The cost depends on the distance driven
The distance depends on the cost
It appears on the right-hand side

subtopics.title: Forward Substitution — Pricing the 340 km Trip

questions.question: The cost of a 340 km trip is:
A learner computes (450 + 12,50) × 340 = R157 250. What went wrong?
options: Order of operations — multiplication must happen before addition

questions.question: Why should the formula and the substitution line be written out before calculating?
options: Each written line typically earns its own mark and lets the marker follow your method
It is required by the calculator

questions.question: Which sense check confirms R4 700 is plausible for the 340 km trip?
options: The driving charge (R4 250) should far exceed the fixed fee (R450) on a long trip — and it does
The answer should be less than R450

subtopics.title: Reverse Substitution — How Far Does R1 200 Go?

questions.question: With a budget of R1 200, the first step after substituting is:
options: Subtract the R450 fixed charge from both sides, leaving R750 for driving

questions.question: Dividing the whole R1 200 by R12,50 gives 96 km. Why is this wrong?
options: R450 of the budget pays the fixed fee and never buys kilometres — it must be removed first

questions.question: How is the answer of 60 km verified?
options: Substitute forwards: 450 + 12,50 × 60 = R1 200, exactly the budget

subtopics.title: The General Method, the Classic Traps, and Where This Skill Lives

questions.question: The correct unwinding order for reverse substitution in a fixed-plus-rate formula is:
options: Subtract the fixed part first, then divide by the rate
Divide by the rate first, then subtract the fixed part
Multiply by the rate, then add the fixed part
Any order gives the same answer

questions.question: A formula requires kilometres but the question gives 4 500 metres. You should:
When should rounding happen in a multi-step substitution?
options: Only at the final answer — carry full values through the working
